title: Debug: Part 2
summary: Trace mutation, aliases, boundaries, and multi-step state.
refresher: Deeper Python bugs often begin before the failing line. Track **object** identity when data is shared, inspect types beside **values**, and test empty, one-item, and boundary inputs.

sections.title: Check whether two names share one object
sections.summary: Mutation bugs often come from two **variables** pointing at the same **list**.

blocks.body: In Python, assignment gives another name to the same object. That is harmless for numbers and **strings** because they do not mutate in place. **Lists** and **dictionaries** are different: if two names point at one list, changing the list through either name changes the same object.

blocks.title: Find the first wrong state
blocks.caption: Compare the expected state with the actual state before the final answer distracts you.

steps.title: Before the update
steps.body: The total is still correct before this loop pass.

steps.title: Wrong update
steps.body: The update changes the wrong variable or uses the wrong operation.

steps.title: Fix the transition
steps.body: Once the first bad transition is known, the fix is smaller.

blocks.caption: The first version prints `[1, 2, 3]` because both names reach the same **list**. The second version **leaves** `original` as `[1, 2]`.
Printing `id` is useful when you need to confirm whether two **variables** name the same **object**.
blocks.code:
a = [1]
b = a
c = a.copy()
print(id(a) == id(b))
print(id(a) == id(c))

blocks.prompt: What does `b = a` do when `a` is a **list**?
choices: converts the list to a tuple
blocks.why: Both names refer to one **list** **object**, so later list mutations are visible through both names.

sections.title: Test the smallest inputs on purpose
sections.summary: Empty and one-item inputs expose assumptions hidden by normal examples.

blocks.body: A bug can hide when every example has several items. Before trusting a **loop**, try the smallest inputs: an empty **list**, a one-item list, and a list where the answer appears at the first or last position.

blocks.caption: Negative indexing is still indexing. `items[-1]` works only when the **list** has at least one element.

blocks.why: An empty **list** has no last element, so the code needs a branch before using `items[-1]`.

sections.title: Find the first wrong state
sections.summary: Debugging gets easier when you stop at the first bad transition.

blocks.caption: **Print** the value before and after the update so you can see exactly which pass changes the state incorrectly.
blocks.code:
total = 0
for score in scores:
    print("before", score, total)
    total += score
    print("after", score, total)

blocks.title: Debug: Part 2 checklist
items: Check whether two names share one **object**.
Log **values** with their types when arithmetic or comparisons look odd.
Find the first line where the state changes incorrectly.
